chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:

I said to al-Rida عليه السلام: We used to ask you, before Allah had granted Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام to you, and you would say: Allah will grant me a boy. Now Allah has indeed granted him to you, and our eyes have been delighted. May Allah not show us your day; but if an event should occur, then to whom?
So he gestured with his hand toward Abi Ja‘far عليه السلام, while he was standing before him.
So I said: May I be your ransom, this is a son of three years? He said: And what harm is there to him in that? Isa عليه السلام stood with the Divine Proof while he was a son of three years.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, identified here as the succeeding Imam
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Imam al-Rida عليه السلام, the one being addressed in the report
key_terms.بِالْحُجَّةِ: with the Divine Proof; bearing divinely granted authority
key_terms.عِيسَى: Isa عليه السلام, cited as a precedent for authority in childhood
key_terms.غُلَامًا: a boy; the promised son granted by Allah
key_terms.يَوْمَكَ: your day; meaning the day of death or passing

ai.seo_question: Can an Imam hold divine authority at a very young age?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the designation of Imam al-Jawad عليه السلام by Imam al-Rida عليه السلام despite his very young age. It presents age as no obstacle to divine authority, drawing a parallel with Isa عليه السلام, who bore the hujjah while still a child.
